the Executive Council, wrote for tlie June, 1930, issue of The

"While mere scholastic marks are not conclusive evidence of
well rounded development, they are academic tests of the charac
ter of curricular work. To fail to meet them, to the extent at least, of
a fair average, is
usually a failure of character, not because schol
arship has not been attained, but because one has started some
thing worth while and has failed to finish it. Psi Upsilon
expects its share of scholars, and has always had them. It ex
pects its share of extra-curricular leaders, and has always had
them also. It demands neither from any members.
"It does, however, demand and expect that every member will
maintain an average of mental life, scholastic work, conduct and
personal relations of a sufficiently high standard to be acceptable
as conclusive evidence
of the rounded development of character,
mind and personality. The doing of things that are not always
pleasing, but because they are right and because doing them is
'playing the game,' makes character. The addition of kindliness,
courtesy, courage and other qualities that come from the heart
make fine men, and so we come back to the
beginning, and the
crowning glory of Psi Upsilon, true friendship between fine
men."

A ten point program for improving conditions in Brown
University fraternities was suggested by Assistant Dean Edgar
J. Lanpher last night before presidents of chapter houses, mem
bers of the student council and the interfraternity governing
board. The points in the administration's platform of "possibili
ties" included:
{1) More power and responsibility to the interfraternity gov
erning board; {2) Either earlier pledging, or pledging deferred to
the sophomore year; {3) Elimination of hazing and undignified
practices in initiations; {4) Improved educational value of fra
ternities; {5) Social life in fraternities maintained consistent
with accepted social standards. Changed practice in the matter
of bars and chaperons; (6) Co-ordinated and more efficient
chapter house finance, through a special officer of the university
or through a man employed for the purpose by the governing

board; (7) Closer supervision by Alumni: {8) Increase of house
solidarity by limitation of the size of houses to 4-0 or 60 men;
{9) Broader interfraternity contacts; {10) Scholastic standards
raised by having a resident tutor in each house. Chapters with
low averages to be deprived of social privileges.
